scholars: Ibn Kathir explains: Al-Asr is the time when people do things, good or bad. Allah swears by it. Another scholar, Zayd ibn Aslam, said it means the evening.

The book Al-Jalalayn says Al-Asr can mean the time from when the sun starts to go down until sunset, or the afternoon prayer. The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says Allah swears by the Asr prayer, or by the hard times of life.

Ibn Kathir tells a story. A man named Musaylimah, who lied and said he was a prophet, asked Amr ibn al-As what had come down to the Prophet ﷺ. Amr read him this surah. Musaylimah tried to make up something like it, but it was silly nonsense about a small animal. Amr told him, 'You know that I know you are lying.'
Ibn Kathir says man is in 'khusr.' That means loss and destruction.

The book Al-Jalalayn says man loses in all of his business. The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says it means that a person who does not believe is in loss, because he loses his family and his place in Paradise. It also says people can lose because their good work gets less when they are old, and stops when they die.
Ibn Kathir explains: Allah makes an exception. People who believe in their hearts and do good things with their bodies are not in loss.

'Tell each other to follow the truth' means to tell each other to obey Allah and stay away from what Allah forbids. 'Tell each other to be patient' means to be patient when people try to hurt you because you tell them to do good and stop doing bad. (Ibn Kathir.)
Ibn Kathir writes that when two of the Prophet's friends met, they did not part until one of them had read Surah Al-Asr to the other, and they had said salaam to each other. (At-Tabarani.)
The great scholar Ash-Shafi'i said: 'If people thought deeply about this surah, it would be enough for them.' (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
